questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to: DOCTOR : PATIENT
questions.explanation: A doctor provides professional service to a patient, just as a lawyer provides professional service to a client. 'Teacher : School' is wrong because school is a place, not the recipient of service. 'Judge : Prison' is wrong because a judge does not serve the prison. 'Nurse : Medicine' is wrong because medicine is a tool, not a person receiving service.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about verbal analogies:

(i) A verbal analogy expresses a relationship between two words or concepts.
(ii) The relationship in the given pair must be exactly mirrored in the answer pair.
(iii) Analogies always involve synonyms or antonyms only.
(iv) Understanding the precise relationship (cause-effect, part-whole, worker-tool, etc.) is key to solving analogies.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. Verbal analogies express relationships between words, require mirroring of the exact relationship, and rely on identifying specific relationship types. Statement (iii) is wrong because analogies can involve many relationship types beyond synonyms and antonyms — such as part-whole, cause-effect, worker-tool, degree, and category-member.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to: PEN : WRITER
questions.explanation: A pen is the tool used by a writer, just as a brush is the tool used by a painter. 'Book : Reader' is wrong because a book is the product consumed, not the tool used by the reader. 'Stage : Actor' is wrong because a stage is the workplace, not a tool. 'Chalk : Classroom' is wrong because classroom is a place, not the person using the tool.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the analogy FISH : WATER :: BIRD : AIR, the relationship is organism to its medium of movement.
Reason (R): Analogies require identifying the exact logical relationship between the first pair and applying it to the second pair.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct because fish moves through water and bird moves through air — the relationship is organism to medium. Reason (R) is correct because solving analogies indeed requires identifying and applying the exact logical relationship. (R) explains (A) because it is precisely by applying this method that we confirm the organism-to-medium relationship in the given analogy.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following analogies with their relationship types:

Column I:
(a) Cow : Calf
(b) Hammer : Nail
(c) Seed : Tree
(d) Captain : Ship

Column II:
(i) Tool and its object
(ii) Leader and what is led
(iii) Parent and offspring
(iv) Cause and effect / growth

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Cow : Calf is parent and offspring (iii). Hammer : Nail is tool and its object (i). Seed : Tree is cause and effect / growth (iv). Captain : Ship is leader and what is led (ii). The second option is wrong because it incorrectly pairs hammer with leader. The third option is wrong because it incorrectly pairs cow with cause-effect. The fourth option is wrong because it incorrectly pairs cow with tool.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to: TEACHER : CLASSROOM
questions.explanation: A teacher works in a classroom, just as a chef works in a kitchen — the relationship is worker to workplace. 'Farmer : Crop' is wrong because crop is the product, not the workplace. 'Singer : Song' is wrong because a song is the output/product. 'Pilot : Journey' is wrong because journey is the activity, not the workplace.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following pairs share the same relationship as LION : PRIDE?

(i) Fish : School
(ii) Cow : Herd
(iii) Dog : Kennel
(iv) Wolf : Pack

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The relationship is animal to its collective noun (group name). Fish : School (i), Cow : Herd (ii), and Wolf : Pack (iv) all express animal to group name. Dog : Kennel (iii) is wrong because a kennel is the shelter/dwelling of a dog, not the collective noun for a group of dogs.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to: EYE : SEE
questions.explanation: An eye is the organ used to see, just as an ear is the organ used to hear — the relationship is organ to its function. 'Hand : Finger' is wrong because finger is a part of the hand, not its function. 'Nose : Face' is wrong because face is the location, not the function. 'Mouth : Teeth' is wrong because teeth are a part within the mouth, not the function of the mouth.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the analogy CHAPTER : BOOK:

(i) The relationship is part to whole.
(ii) A similar analogy would be Verse : Poem.
(iii) The relationship is synonymous — chapter means the same as book.
(iv) A similar analogy would be Room : House.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — a chapter is a part of a book. Statement (ii) is correct — a verse is a part of a poem. Statement (iv) is correct — a room is a part of a house. Statement (iii) is wrong because chapter and book are not synonyms; they have a part-to-whole relationship, not a same-meaning relationship.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to: NEEDLE : THREAD
questions.explanation: A needle has a thread passed through it to function (they work together as complementary items where one passes through the other). Similarly, a shoe has a lace passed through it to function. 'Lock : Key' is wrong because a key opens a lock — it's a mechanism relationship, not a threading-through relationship. 'Paper : Ink' is wrong because ink is applied on paper. 'Hammer : Wood' is wrong because hammer strikes wood — it's a tool-material relationship.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): MARATHON : RACE is an example of a type-to-category analogy.
Reason (R): A marathon is a specific type of race, showing the relationship of specific to general.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct because marathon is indeed a type of race — specific to general/category. Reason (R) is correct because it accurately explains that a marathon is a specific variety within the broader category of races. (R) directly explains why (A) is a type-to-category analogy. The other options are wrong because both statements are factually correct and (R) provides the logical basis for (A).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to: CALM : STORM
questions.explanation: Calm is the opposite of storm, just as peace is the opposite of war — the relationship is antonym. 'Dark : Night' is wrong because dark is a characteristic of night, not its opposite. 'Hot : Summer' is wrong because hot is a quality associated with summer, not its opposite. 'Rain : Cloud' is wrong because rain comes from a cloud — it's a cause-effect relationship, not antonyms.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following word pairs with their analogy types:

Column I:
(a) Germ : Disease
(b) Knife : Cut
(c) Puppy : Dog
(d) Brave : Cowardly

Column II:
(i) Young to adult
(ii) Cause and effect
(iii) Tool and its action
(iv) Antonym pair

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Germ : Disease is cause and effect (ii) — germs cause disease. Knife : Cut is tool and its action (iii) — a knife is used to cut. Puppy : Dog is young to adult (i) — a puppy grows into a dog. Brave : Cowardly is antonym pair (iv) — they have opposite meanings. The second option wrongly swaps germ and knife relationships. The third option wrongly assigns puppy to antonym. The fourth option wrongly assigns germ to antonym.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to: GALAXY : STARS
questions.explanation: A galaxy is a collection of stars, just as a bouquet is a collection of flowers — the relationship is collection to its components. 'Ocean : Ship' is wrong because a ship travels on the ocean, it is not a component of it. 'Library : Reader' is wrong because a reader uses the library, not makes up the library. 'Garden : Gardener' is wrong because a gardener tends the garden, not constitutes it.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the analogy AUTHOR : NOVEL:

(i) The relationship is creator to creation.
(ii) Composer : Symphony shares the same relationship.
(iii) Painter : Gallery shares the same relationship.
(iv) Architect : Building shares the same relationship.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — an author creates a novel. Statement (ii) is correct — a composer creates a symphony. Statement (iv) is correct — an architect creates/designs a building. Statement (iii) is wrong because a painter does not create a gallery; a gallery is the place where paintings are displayed, not something the painter creates. A correct analogy would be Painter : Painting.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to: FLOCK : SHEEP
questions.explanation: A flock is the collective noun for sheep, just as a swarm is the collective noun for bees — the relationship is group name to the animal. 'Forest : Tiger' is wrong because forest is the habitat, not a group name. 'Pond : Fish' is wrong because pond is the habitat. 'Cage : Parrot' is wrong because a cage is the enclosure, not a collective noun.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: GLOVE : HAND :: SOCK : __________
questions.explanation: A glove is worn on the hand, just as a sock is worn on the foot. 'Shoe' is wrong because a shoe goes over the sock, not a body part that the sock covers. 'Leg' is wrong because a sock does not cover the entire leg. 'Ankle' is wrong because a sock covers the foot primarily, not just the ankle.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to: THERMOMETER : TEMPERATURE
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature, just as a barometer measures (atmospheric) pressure — the relationship is instrument to what it measures. 'Stethoscope : Doctor' is wrong because it's an instrument to user relationship, not instrument to measurement. 'Telescope : Star' is wrong because a telescope is used to observe stars, not to measure them. 'Clock : Wall' is wrong because wall is where a clock is placed, not what it measures.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following pairs share the same relationship as HOSPITAL : DOCTOR?

(i) Court : Judge
(ii) School : Teacher
(iii) Office : Computer
(iv) Laboratory : Scientist

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The relationship is workplace to the professional who works there. Court : Judge (i), School : Teacher (ii), and Laboratory : Scientist (iv) all express workplace to professional. Office : Computer (iii) is wrong because a computer is equipment found in an office, not a professional who works there.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): KITTEN : CAT :: CYGNET : SWAN is a valid analogy.
Reason (R): Both pairs express the relationship of young animal to its adult form.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — kitten is a young cat, and cygnet is a young swan, so the analogy is valid. Reason (R) is correct — it accurately identifies the young-to-adult relationship. (R) explains (A) because the analogy is valid precisely because both pairs share the young-to-adult relationship. The other options are wrong as both statements are correct and logically connected.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to: ISLAND : OCEAN
questions.explanation: An island is a small area of land surrounded by ocean, just as an oasis is a small fertile area surrounded by desert — the relationship is a smaller distinct entity within a larger surrounding. 'Mountain : Valley' is wrong because a mountain is not surrounded by valley in the same way. 'River : Bridge' is wrong because a bridge crosses a river — it's not surrounded by it. 'Forest : Village' is wrong because a village is not necessarily surrounded by forest.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to: ACTOR : THEATRE
questions.explanation: An actor performs in a theatre, just as an athlete performs in a stadium — the relationship is performer to performance venue. 'Singer : Music' is wrong because music is what a singer produces, not the venue. 'Dancer : Grace' is wrong because grace is a quality, not a venue. 'Player : Victory' is wrong because victory is an outcome, not a place of performance.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about analogy types:

(i) SWORD : WARRIOR is an example of a tool-to-user relationship.
(ii) MILK : WHITE is an example of an object-to-its-characteristic relationship.
(iii) MANGO : FRUIT is an example of a specific-to-general (type-category) relationship.
(iv) KING : QUEEN is an example of a synonym relationship.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — a sword is the tool used by a warrior. Statement (ii) is correct — white is the characteristic colour of milk. Statement (iii) is correct — mango is a specific type within the general category fruit. Statement (iv) is wrong because king and queen are not synonyms; they represent male and female counterparts (gender relationship), not words with the same meaning.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to: LIGHT : DARKNESS
questions.explanation: Light is the opposite of darkness, just as noise is the opposite of silence — the relationship is antonym. 'Water : River' is wrong because water is the substance that makes up a river — it's a component relationship, not an antonym. 'Heat : Fire' is wrong because heat is produced by fire — it's a cause-effect relationship. 'Wind : Storm' is wrong because wind is a component of a storm, not its opposite.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following analogies with the correct second term:

Column I:
(a) Bird : Nest :: Rabbit : ?
(b) Cow : Milk :: Hen : ?
(c) Sheep : Wool :: Silkworm : ?
(d) Horse : Stable :: Dog : ?

Column II:
(i) Kennel
(ii) Silk
(iii) Burrow
(iv) Egg

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Bird lives in a nest, rabbit lives in a burrow (iii). Cow gives milk, hen gives eggs (iv). Sheep gives wool, silkworm gives silk (ii). Horse lives in a stable, dog lives in a kennel (i). The second option wrongly assigns kennel to rabbit. The third option wrongly assigns egg to silkworm. The fourth option wrongly assigns egg to rabbit.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to: PLAGIARISM : WRITING
questions.explanation: Plagiarism is the act of copying or stealing in the domain of writing, just as forgery is the act of copying or faking in the domain of painting/art — the relationship is a dishonest act to the field in which it is committed. 'Reading : Library' is wrong because reading is a legitimate activity done at a library. 'Singing : Concert' is wrong because singing is the legitimate activity performed at a concert. 'Cooking : Recipe' is wrong because cooking using a recipe is a normal and honest activity.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the analogy OXYGEN : BREATHING:

(i) The relationship is substance needed for a process.
(ii) Water : Swimming shares the same relationship.
(iii) Fuel : Engine shares a similar relationship.
(iv) Light : Photosynthesis shares a similar relationship.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — oxygen is the substance required for the process of breathing. Statement (iii) is correct — fuel is the substance required for an engine to function. Statement (iv) is correct — light is the substance/energy required for the process of photosynthesis. Statement (ii) is wrong because water is the medium in which swimming takes place, not a substance consumed by the process of swimming.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to: FOOD : HUNGER
questions.explanation: Food satisfies hunger, just as water satisfies thirst — the relationship is something that removes/satisfies a need. 'Sleep : Pillow' is wrong because a pillow aids sleep but does not satisfy it as a need in the same way. 'Medicine : Pharmacy' is wrong because a pharmacy is where medicine is sold, not the need it satisfies. 'Cloth : Tailor' is wrong because a tailor works with cloth — it's a worker-material relationship, not a satisfier-need relationship.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following pairs share the same relationship as CHAPTER : BOOK?

(i) Stanza : Poem
(ii) Scene : Play
(iii) Page : Ink
(iv) Act : Drama

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The relationship is a subdivision/part to the whole literary work. Stanza : Poem (i), Scene : Play (ii), and Act : Drama (iv) all express a structural part of a literary/dramatic work to the whole work. Page : Ink (iii) is wrong because ink is the material on a page, not a structural subdivision of it — and page-to-ink is not a part-to-whole-literary-work relationship.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to: CLOTH : TAILOR
questions.explanation: Cloth is the material worked upon by a tailor, just as wood is the material worked upon by a carpenter — the relationship is raw material to the craftsman who uses it. 'Brick : House' is wrong because house is the finished product made from bricks, not the craftsman. 'Iron : Heavy' is wrong because heavy is a property of iron, not a craftsman. 'Stone : Mountain' is wrong because mountain is made of stone naturally, not by a craftsman.
